assessment.summary: The three surviving contact findings share one admission-control boundary; centralizing cheap route checks and pairing them with a deployment-edge global quota is proportionate to this static portfolio.

nonNegotiables: Preserve the rendered design, animation timing, transitions, and valid contact-form behavior.
Avoid adding a new paid or stateful service without explicit approval.
assumptions: No measured provider-latency or production traffic budget was supplied.

opportunities.title: Own contact admission at one boundary
opportunities.summary: Consolidate request authority, configuration validity, resource bounds, and provider deadlines before email delivery, with the global quota enforced at the deployment edge.
opportunities.diagnosis: The route currently mixes browser authority, optional-control configuration, process-local state, parsing, and provider delivery. Two findings arise from missing local admission checks; the third arises because a global quota is assigned to instance-local memory.

evidence.claim: A missing Turnstile secret is treated as successful verification even when the client can advertise Turnstile.
The five-per-hour budget is stored in a module-local Map and is not shared across serverless instances.
The route parses hostile-origin text/plain JSON without a request-authority gate.
A single cheap admission phase before parsing and upstream I/O can own the local invariants, while only an edge or durable service can own a global quota.

desiredInvariants: Every browser contact submission is same-origin application/json before its body is parsed.
Turnstile is either deliberately disabled or fully paired; partial configuration and provider failure never authorize delivery.
Every request has a bounded body, bounded local state cost, and bounded upstream wait.
Production enforces one authoritative per-client contact budget across all function instances.

options.title: Layered route admission plus Vercel Firewall
options.summary: Add one route-owned admission pipeline and bounded local burst guard, then make a path-specific platform-edge rule the authoritative shared rate limit.

findingCoverage.rationale: Paired configuration and fail-closed verification directly repair the route.
Same-origin and JSON gates directly repair the route.
The platform rule is authoritative; the bounded Map remains only a secondary burst guard.

tradeoffs.assessment: One owned route admission gate closes the configuration and origin failures; an edge rule supplies the missing shared quota boundary.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run route regression tests, re-run all three local PoCs, and verify the production firewall rule and response headers.

tradeoffs.assessment: Cheap media-type, origin, and byte-length checks reject abusive requests before JSON parsing or upstream I/O; the edge rule can reject before function execution.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare local Lighthouse and contact rejection latency before and after, and inspect Vercel function invocations after rollout.

tradeoffs.assessment: A capped, swept burst-guard Map prevents unbounded process-local key retention; no new application cache is introduced.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Unit-test the limiter cap and observe heap behavior under a synthetic high-cardinality local workload.

tradeoffs.assessment: Provider timeouts and fail-closed configuration make failure bounded and predictable while same-origin valid submissions retain the existing path.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Mock Cloudflare and Resend timeouts, errors, and success responses and verify deterministic status codes.

tradeoffs.assessment: The code remains self-contained, but production correctness depends on a documented Vercel Firewall rule and environment-pair validation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Add the rule and environment checklist to deployment runbooks and verify them after every production deployment.

tradeoffs.assessment: The public UI and valid same-origin JSON contract are unchanged; only abusive and misconfigured paths change.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run the existing contact UI through the browser and verify no DOM, animation, or request-shape regression.

residualRisks: The global quota remains unverified until the production Vercel Firewall rule is inspected and enabled.
The CSP retains unsafe-inline for framework bootstrap and existing inline styles to preserve static rendering and visual behavior.

workPackages: Centralize pre-parse admission checks and response policy.
Bound local state and all upstream waits.
Add regression tests and document the required edge rule.
acceptanceCriteria: All local finding PoCs are rejected or model the repaired invariant.
Valid same-origin submissions preserve their current UI contract.
Production headers and the edge rate-limit rule are verified.
migrationNotes: No response-shape or visible UI change is intended.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert the focused route/config commit and disable the edge rule if legitimate contact traffic is blocked.

options.title: Atomic durable application limiter
options.summary: Keep the route admission gate but replace process-local quota authority with an atomic managed rate-limit store called by the function.

findingCoverage.rationale: The local paired-configuration patch remains required.
The local request-authority patch remains required.
An atomic shared store becomes the authoritative global budget.

tradeoffs.assessment: An atomic durable limiter makes the global quota explicit in application code while the same local admission gate closes origin and configuration failures.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise multi-instance concurrency against a disposable durable store and re-run all local finding PoCs.

tradeoffs.assessment: Every accepted candidate request gains a network round trip to the limiter unless a platform-local service is selected.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure p50 and p95 contact submission latency and set a rollback threshold before production.

tradeoffs.assessment: Application memory remains bounded; state moves to a managed external service.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inspect local heap and provider key cardinality/TTL behavior under synthetic traffic.

tradeoffs.assessment: Atomic shared state improves quota correctness but adds a provider dependency and requires an explicit fail-closed or degraded-mode decision.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fault-inject limiter timeouts and verify the selected failure policy.

tradeoffs.assessment: A new credential, service, retention policy, monitoring surface, and possible billable dependency must be operated.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Complete credential rotation, alerting, quota, and incident-response checks before enabling.

tradeoffs.assessment: The route, tests, deployment variables, and infrastructure configuration all change.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Canary the limiter behind a feature flag and retain the edge rule for rollback.

residualRisks: Limiter availability becomes part of contact availability.
Credential and provider misconfiguration create a new operational failure mode.

workPackages: Select and provision an atomic store.
Integrate behind a narrow limiter interface.
Canary with edge fallback and fault-injection tests.
acceptanceCriteria: Concurrent cross-instance request six is rejected atomically.
Limiter failure follows an explicit tested policy.
migrationNotes: Requires a new external service and secrets.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable the durable limiter feature flag and retain the platform-edge rule.

opportunities.recommendation: Use layered route admission plus the Vercel Firewall under the current static-site, low-traffic, no-new-service constraints. Move to a durable store only if product requirements demand application-owned quotas or richer identity-based policy.

openQuestions: Which production Vercel Firewall rule and threshold are currently active for POST /api/contact?
Should a future custom domain become the only accepted Origin, or should the canonical vercel.app alias remain valid?
